To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the regional distribution (topographic) of gas transport during high-frequency oscillations is dependent on lung volumes, with gas transport to the bases of the lung being more dependent on lung volume than gas transport to the apices of the lung.
the regional distribution during HFO depends on the volume of gas in the lung and that gas is distributed more uniformly to the bases of the lung than to the apices.
during high frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV) the distribution of gas is dependent on lung volumes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of lung volume upon the regional gas transport during HFO.
the effects of lung inflation and oscillation frequency on the distribution of HFO ventilation.
the effects of lung inflation on regional gas transport and regional ventilation during high frequency oscillatory ventilation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regional distribution is dependent upon the lung volume, but the mechanism is still unclear.
HFO ventilation is not as efficient at low lung volumes, but that it can be used safely and effectively at FRC or above.
the distribution of gas transport is dependent upon lung volume, with the greatest distribution of gas occurring at FRC, and the least occurring at RV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HFO gas transport to topographical regions in the lungs is dependent on lung volumes and that this dependency is related to the relative contributions of convection and diffusion.
the regional distribution and transport of gas by HFO are determined by the lung volume at which HFO is performed, the frequency, and the oscillatory volume.
the gas transport efficiency of HFO is volume dependent, with the highest efficiency occurring in the upper lung zones, and the efficiency progressively decreases as one moves down the lung.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HFO gas transport to the base of the lung is more efficient at FRC than at RV.
the distribution of gas during HFO is dependent on the distribution of the oscillatory volume.
the distribution of gas during HFO is volume-dependent.
